answer: An agent economy resists sybils by requiring each identity to lock a refundable stake before it can transact or vote. A thousand fake personas therefore demand a thousand separate stakes, so an attacker’s influence stays fixed while his capital at risk multiplies. Peers then review every identity’s public work trail the way a falcon scans a dune for motion, and any colluding identity gets its stake slashed. Because launching each duplicate is a fresh voyage that costs a full new bond, mass fabrication becomes strictly unprofitable.
